summary_paragraph: A 65-year-old male with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, coronary artery disease, and type 2 diabetes was admitted for left-sided chest pain associated with severe hyperkalemia (potassium 7.1) and EKG changes. He received emergency treatment with calcium gluconate and underwent emergent hemodialysis, which improved his symptoms and normalized potassium. Serial troponins were stable, ruling out acute myocardial infarction. He remained chest pain-free, completed a second dialysis session, and was discharged home in stable condition. The rise in potassium was not clearly due to dietary indiscretion; nephrology will evaluate for underlying causes such as hypoaldosteronism. Medications were adjusted, including increasing lisinopril and adding docusate, and low-potassium diet counseling was provided.
problems: Diabetes with renal manifestations, type II or unspecified type, not stated as uncontrolled
